facts.text: Murray City was named after John Murray Brown, the original landowner who built a hotel in 1875.
The village was platted in 1873, incorporated in 1891, and grew rapidly because of coal mining, becoming one of the largest coal towns in the Hocking Valley.
A preserved red train caboose and the historic Murray City Train Depot once served as the town’s sole link to the Hocking Valley Railway, carrying coal and people.
Philip Neri Catholic Church, founded in 1903, sits on a hilltop and is one of the first buildings seen descending from Murray City Hill.
In the 1920s, Murray City fielded a semi‑professional football team called the Murray City Tigers, a nod to the town’s early sports culture.
The village lies along the Snow Fork, a tributary of Monday Creek, winding through the rolling hills of the Hocking Valley.
